get.summary: Returns the antiforgery token to send with every unsafe request, and sets its cookie. Request a new token after signing in or out.

post.summary: Registers a user and a new organization that the user owns. The user must then sign in.
Signs in with e-mail and password and starts a cookie session.

get.summary: Returns the signed-in user, their organization and role.
Gets an organization.

put.summary: Replaces an organization's settings: name, time zone and the optional overdue materiality threshold (the smallest overdue customer balance, in the organization's currency, worth an insight; absent clears it and then every overdue balance is reported). The currency cannot be changed.

post.summary: Creates a product. Prices are in the organization's currency. A SKU that exists in any letter case is a conflict.

get.summary: Lists products, one page at a time (page size 1 to 100, default 25), optionally matching part of the SKU or name. Inactive products are left out unless includeInactive is true.
Gets a product. The cost price is null for callers who may not see costs.

post.summary: Takes a product out of use. Products are never deleted. Deactivating an inactive product changes nothing.
Creates a customer. Credit terms are the number of days until a balance is overdue (0 to 365), optional.

get.summary: Lists customers by name, one page at a time (page size 1 to 100, default 25), optionally matching part of the name. Inactive customers are left out unless includeInactive is true. Contact details are null for callers who may not manage customers.
Gets a customer. Contact details are null for callers who may not manage customers.

put.summary: Replaces a customer's name, contact details and credit terms. An absent contact or credit terms clears it.

post.summary: Takes a customer out of use. Customers are never deleted. Deactivating an inactive customer changes nothing.

get.summary: What a customer owes: the total outstanding and the overdue part, and the sales on account that still owe something (earliest due first). Derived from the sales and payment records on every request, never stored. A sale is overdue when its due date has passed.
Lists the organization's audit events, newest first, one page at a time (page size 1 to 100, default 25). Owner only. Filters are optional and exact; from is inclusive, to is exclusive.

post.summary: Adjusts a product's stock by hand. A note is required. Sending the same adjustmentId again changes nothing and answers 200 with alreadyRecorded true. Removing more than exists is 422.

get.summary: Lists the stock of the active products, by name, optionally those matching part of the SKU or name (page size 1 to 100, default 25). A product that has never had stock shows 0. Same figures and the same definition of low as GetStockLevel.
Gets a product's stock (0 if it has never had stock) and whether it is low.
Lists active products with reorder settings whose stock is at or below the reorder point, the emptiest first (page size 1 to 100, default 25).
Lists a product's stock movements, newest first (page size 1 to 100, default 25). Owner and Manager only.
Lists suppliers by name (page size 1 to 100, default 25). Inactive suppliers are left out unless includeInactive is true.

post.summary: Creates a draft purchase order with its lines. Unit costs are in the organization's currency, which the order takes; a currency or a total in the request is not read. The product's SKU, name and unit are recorded on the line.

get.summary: Lists purchase orders, newest first, optionally of one status or supplier (page size 1 to 100, default 25).
Gets a purchase order with its lines and received quantities.

post.summary: Places a draft order with the supplier. Only a draft can be placed (422 otherwise).
Cancels a draft or placed order that has received nothing (422 otherwise).

Records goods received against lines of a placed or partially received order and adds the stock, atomically. Sending the same receiptId again with exactly the same order, lines and quantities changes nothing and answers 200 with alreadyRecorded true; the same receiptId with anything different is 409 (purchase_order.receipt_id_conflict). Receiving more than is outstanding is 422.

Records a sale and removes the stock, atomically. Lines are charged the catalog price; a line may state the final unitPrice (an override or a discount, never negative) with a priceReason, which needs the SalesOverridePrice permission (Owner and Manager), and a price below the product's cost needs SalesSellBelowCost (Owner), else 403. The catalog price, the price charged, the reason and the user are recorded and a price override is audited. Costs and totals are taken and computed by the server. With a customerId it is a sale on account: amountPaid is what the customer pays now (0 up to the total; absent means paid in full), the rest is owed from a due date fixed now (sale date plus the customer's credit terms, or immediately). Without a customer the sale is paid in full. Sending the same saleId again with exactly the same products, quantities, prices, reasons, customer and amount paid changes nothing and answers 200 with alreadyRecorded true; the same saleId with anything different is 409 (sale.id_conflict). Selling more than is in stock is 422. A sale recorded offline (synchronization after an outage) also sends occurredAtUtc, the offlineGrantId that vouches for it and, on every line, catalogPriceShown (the catalog price the cashier saw). The server accepts occurredAtUtc only inside a silent gap it observed on that grant, within the offline window (72 hours by default, from the start of the gap), not in the future (a small clock-skew allowance that never widens a gap), and the grant must be the caller's and not revoked; otherwise nothing is recorded, no id is reserved and the sale is never dated at server time (409 offline.event_time_unverifiable / offline.event_time_outside_window / offline.grant_*, 400 offline.event_time_in_future). A catalogPriceShown different from the current catalog price is 409 sale.catalog_price_changed (the final unitPrice is never compared). The server records its own receipt time. The server cannot prove a device was physically offline, only that it observed no contact.

get.summary: Lists sales, newest first, optionally of one status (page size 1 to 100, default 25).
Gets a sale with its lines. Cost prices are shown only to callers who may see costs.

post.summary: Voids a completed sale with a required reason and returns its stock, atomically. A sale can be voided once (422 otherwise). Owner and Manager only.

Records a payment received against a sale made on account. Money is recorded, never processed. The amount cannot be more than what is still owed (422). paidAtUtc is when the money was received (default now; not before the sale, not in the future). Sending the same paymentId again with exactly the same sale, amount, method and date changes nothing and answers 200 with alreadyRecorded true; the same paymentId with anything different is 409 (sale.payment_id_conflict).

Takes back one recorded payment in full, as a new record that points at it (the payment is never changed). A reason is required. A payment can be reversed once and a reversal cannot be reversed (422). Sending the same reversalId again for the same payment and reason answers 200 with alreadyRecorded true. Owner and Manager only.

get.summary: Revenue and quantity for the last N complete local days (default 30, at most 92) against the N days before them, with top sellers, slow movers and declining products. Voided sales are excluded. Owner and Manager only.

Gross margin (revenue minus the cost price recorded on each sale line) for the last N complete local days (default 30, at most 92) against the N days before them, in total and per product: margin percentage, the change in percentage points, average price and cost, products at a loss, products whose margin fell, and products with no recorded cost (their margin is not guessed). A management measure, not accounting. Needs InsightsView and ProductViewCost (Owner and Manager).

Purchase unit costs from placed purchase orders: per product and supplier, the latest cost against the supplier's previous purchase (a change of at least 10% is notable), the gap between suppliers, and the volume (orders, quantity, spend) of the last N complete local days (default 30, at most 92). A single costed purchase is reported as insufficient history, never as no change. Needs InsightsView and ProductViewCost (Owner and Manager).

What customers owe, as of now: the total outstanding, the part not yet due and the overdue part split into aging buckets (0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 91+ days past the due date, in the organization's calendar), and the most overdue customers with the sales behind each balance. A payment reduces only the sale it was recorded against. Derived from the sales and payment records on every request, never stored. Owner and Manager only.

post.summary: Issues the caller's offline grant after an online validation, replacing their previous one. The grant id is an identifier, not a secret: it does nothing without the caller's session. Needs the permission to record sales or payments; each offline sale and payment is still checked against its own permission when it is sent. The server generates the id and every time; the device clock is never used. The device should then report contact about every 5 minutes (POST .../{id}/contact) while it is online. Honest limit: the server cannot tell a disconnected device from one that stays silent on purpose; it vouches for an offline event time only inside a silent gap it observed.

Reports that the caller's device is in contact; the server records its own clock. 404 offline.grant_not_found (also for another user's or organization's grant), 409 offline.grant_revoked, offline.grant_superseded or offline.grant_expired (ask for a new grant). Contact is append-only: it never changes what earlier silent gaps were.
